reason: Held-out leakage in the attribution's law pick, as the skeptic sharpened it. The steep law (kK 3.0, s_arm 4.0, r_lobe 8.5) was set by hand from a law table counted on Bench(110,360) and the 952 held-out poses (docs/research/longstroke_drive/stroke_curve.py calls held_bench()). On the frozen protocol's own fit objective (Bench(60,160) fast, 2 mm near-touch gap) kK 3.0 ranks LAST of the four laws tried: 16.73, against 15.60 for kK 1.98, 16.35 for 2.3 and 16.22 for 2.65. On plain it is first by only 0.11. So the pick goes against the fit bench, and 21.11 is not a frozen-protocol held-out number. The leak-free attribution, ghost g65d at the CMA's own law, is held out -0.76 against slipper-nose, with a 90 % CI of [-1.91, +0.07] and P 0.933, so its interval crosses 0. The robust '-2.35 held' exists only with the hand-picked steep law. The row's verdict text still quotes the leaky 2.34.

The attribution's held-out gain comes from one pose class, not from the lever, and the row's story still credits the lever. The paired, exact, per-pose numbers are unchanged since the 09:23 audit and were reproduced independently by the skeptic. On the bench the ghost is -0.24 against slipper-nose, CI [-2.12, +1.85], a coin toss. Held out it is -2.35, CI [-3.70, -0.86]. Of its 30 extra held-out poses, 17 sit below elevation 60 (16 of them with |axial| >= 120) and only 3 are overhead (21 vs 18 of 71). The steep law's own share (k30 vs g65d) is +17 / -6 poses: 11 below elevation 60 with |axial| >= 120 and 0 overhead. It also adds 7 contact-only poses in the low-arm, internally rotated class, and deepens the (-90, 60, 120) press from 6.1 to 9.2 mm. The long stroke was meant to win stretched overhead poses at th 110-113, and it does not: overhead most of all is the user's goal.

A stiffer spring felt at the steep law, and no dynamics run on file for this design at any law. The lobe follower is force-closed by K's clock spring (0.08 N.m preload + 0.015 N.m/rad; row red_team.liftoff), and the wearer feels kK x tau_K at J2. On the claim (kK 1.957) that is 0.18 N.m, 1.2-1.5 N at a 150-120 mm cuff. At the ghost's steep law (kK 3.0, K up to 54 deg) it is 0.28 N.m, 1.9-2.35 N. Against REQUIREMENTS R17 (<= 1 N.m peak about the shoulder, <= 5 N and <= 5 deg at the cuff), the static spring alone uses about 28 % and 47 %. K turns 3x as fast as q2 at kK 3.0, so the follower's dynamic hold matters more. No judge/dynamics.py (R17) output exists for longstroke-slipper-knuckle-3r: no file under docs/concepts/verify and no dynamics key in the row. Cuff twist (G3) is therefore unmeasured too. The R17 gate change in 8f69bd6 (unrounded gates) touched no number of this row.
